newsitem.title: USA: USDA cotton exports seen 6.4 mln-6.6 mln bales.
newsitem.headline: USDA cotton exports seen 6.4 mln-6.6 mln bales.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture is expected to raise its forecast for U.S. exports to 6.4 to 6.6 million bales in its monthly supply and demand report, industry analysts said.
Exports were pegged at 6.3 million 480-lb bales in the last report.
The February data will be released Wednesday at 0830 EST.

O.A. Cleveland, a cotton marketing specialist with Mississippi State University, said brisk sales to China coupled with limited supplies outside the United Staes, will prompt the USDA to raise its export forecast to between 6.5 million and 6.6 million bales.
Exports could reach as high as 6.6 million to 6.7 million bales by the end of the season, he added.
Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said shrinking foreign supplies could lift the USDA's export estimate by 100,000 to 200,000 bales, bringing the February forecast to as many as 6.5 million bales.
Exports could climb to 6.8 million bales by the end of the marketing year if prices fall by about 1.50 cents per lb, she added.
The National Cotton Council said exports could reach 6.8 million bales during its annual meeting this weekend, but did not comment on whether the increase would show up in the February report.
Ending stocks would fall to 4.0 million bales by the end of the season, from the current USDA forecast of 4.7 million bales, NCC said.
Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, expects the USDA to keep exports unchanged from its previous forecast at 6.3 million bales.
"We are now shipping at a 6.3 (million bale) rate," Johnson said, adding that the potential exists for the U.S. to export 6.5 million bales by the end of the season.
"Anything above that is just pie in the sky," she said.

The U.S. production figure will remain unchanged from the January estimate at 18.95 million bales. The USDA could revise its output estimate in March when it releases the last report of the 1996/97 crop year.
